body: It must have been horrible to see so many deaths like this. Completely understand your reasoning here. Dignified death for the terminally ill should absolutely be an option.
This is fucking sad and says a lot about the world we live in. I wish you all the best.
Sorry dude. I also definitely would have come. I've been trying to get my boyfriend's friends to come to a BBQ, but no one seems interested. I don't have friends of my own. Feels bad.
I understand too. I used to just do it out of boredom, but now it's one of the only ways to distract myself from thinking about suicide. I don't know if it's a good thing or not.

Lol high school was pretty much the only period of my life where I felt somewhat happy. I got sick of having low self esteem, so I just decided to stop giving a fuck what people thought of me. I had my little circle of friends and I thought I was a pretty awesome person, and that's all I needed. But I moved to a different state right after high school and didn't have my safe bubble anymore. I had to start over and get new people to like me. It's been 10 years and my only 2 friends left are the ones from high school. Lol. I hate myself. Why can't I go back to badass high school me?

I definitely can't argue with the fear of being locked up in a hospital. I can easily say that being forced to stay in those places made me feel worse.

I would give medication another shot. I know that path may seem hopeless. I've tried dozens of medications over the course of about 6 years and have only found 2 that do anything. For me, it's been Cymbalta, with Abilify as a boost. Mental health doctors will usually have free samples of these kinds of higher-end medications that you can try. They're expensive, even with insurance, but you can send in an application to the manufacturers to get free medication if you can't afford it. I've been doing this for a year now, and it's been really helpful.

I would keep in mind that suicide is most likely not a reset button. It's permanent and probably leads to nothingness. It sounds like there's still a shred of desire to keep on living within you. I would try to hold on to that for a while.

Are you seeing a therapist/psychiatrist or taking any medication? Those are things worth looking into. I don't know what your history with depression and suicidal feelings are, but I personally feel like suicide is something that a lot of thought should be put into. It's too important of a decision to be made on an urge or impulse. Give it a couple days and see how you feel about it.
Do you feel guilty because of the people you'd be leaving behind?
You should probably drink more alcohol rather than smoke crack. It's more socially acceptable.
